residuals.statement: The kernel's settlement proof is an exact observed decrease of its own balance. A recipient-side fee settles, and a balanceOf that lies by exactly the expected debit settles with nothing moved and the nonce burned. An issuer can debit the clone on its own ledger with no kernel act at all, by seizure or a downward rebase, can blocklist the clone itself, which stops its spend and egress until lifted (the one case architecture 13.4 keeps, and D-5), and can change any of this for every vault at once by upgrade. No kernel check can close these: asset admission must. A false-returning token that moves settles too, because the boolean is trusted in neither direction. Custody names blocklisting and freezing; 'Issuer controls are external' is the class, and the owner's lane requirements 6 and 12 place the rest of it on asset admission.
